text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- Partial oil exports first step on path of lifting all trade curbs on Iraq.
- Tunis to supply Iraq with foodstuffs.
- Turkish offer for the sale of sugar to Iraq.
- Moslems in Britain welcome the flow of Iraq oil.
- Iraqis in Hungary congratulate President Saddam Hussein on safety of his son.
- Italian businessmen to visit Iraq.
- National Assembly passes law on setting up private and mixed-sector companies.
- Ministry of Industry draws plans for the manufacture of 500 computers and Trade Ministry allows Iraqis living abroad to bring a laptop into the country.
- Justice minister meets Qatari ambassador.
(The above were also carried by AL-JUMHOURIYA and AL-THAWRA)
JUMHOURIYA
- Turkey expands its trade with Iraq.
- More foreign offers to supply Iraq with foodstuffs.
- Ministry of Industry to supply farmers with tractor tyres.
- More land reclaimed in southern Iraq.
- Construction of 13 mosques in Nineveh province.
THAWRA
- Editorial says U.S. denial of having a CIA network in Iraq is groundless.
